intent.tagline: The habit-hooks scan reports 2,340 findings. This program names them in one catalog, clears the viewer, and holds the rest in a second epic.
intent.narration: ADR-0038 made the habit-hooks scan a standing check that review and maintenance run. A standing check that only reports never resolves. The scan holds 2,340 findings across 14 smells, and 1,637 of them sit in the viewer. The engineer excluded the generated viewer folders, which removed 119 findings. This program writes one catalog, clears the viewer in seven slices, and keeps the other 703 findings in a second epic that a later pass cuts.

problem_solution.problem: The standing scan reports 2,340 findings across 14 smells, and none is resolved or named for the next person to take. The viewer holds 1,637 of them in 70 files that top every limit at once.
problem_solution.solution: One catalog clusters the findings and gives each cluster a verdict. The first epic clears the viewer by area, logic first, and ends with its comments. The second epic holds the rest.
problem_solution.narration: The catalog turns the scan into work. It lists all 14 smells with their counts and groups them into seven clusters: structural, type surface, hygiene, duplicates, Python exceptions, comment habit, and React lint. The first epic takes every viewer finding. It starts with the logic layer, because pure logic proves a split keeps behavior with the test suite alone. Then it takes the atoms and sections, the change surface, the shell and chrome, the test files, and the comments. Each slice keeps the export names and re-exports the moved units. The scan is the verifier: a viewer file is done when habit-sensors reports no finding for it. The second epic holds the 703 findings outside the viewer, with a count and an approach for each group.

beats.text: A standing check that reports 2,340 findings but names none of them leaves the next engineer to re-run the scan and re-judge every cluster.
ADR-0016 keeps the plugins as a bundle seam, so the first epic stays inside one district, the viewer under plugins/artifact/viewer/.
The viewer's public surface, its model, atom, section, and hook exports, is the contract the tests and the other files import.
Split by area, logic first. The logic slice proves the export-stability contract and the byte-equal rebuild guard before a render slice depends on them.
The 12-line function limit is a recorded exception. A 13-to-30-line component or test callback that is one unit may stay, and the catalog names it.
The last two slices remove the comments, one comment at a time. A comment that explains why stays, reworded if needed, and a reviewer samples the result.
A split that moves an export breaks the tests that import it. The abort condition on a moved export guards every slice.

alternatives.option: Tune the sensor card for the viewer instead of refactoring to the limits
alternatives.rejected_because: It hides the debt behind a higher limit and leaves 1,560-line files.

alternatives.option: Split by smell, one epic per smell across the whole repo
alternatives.rejected_because: It reopens each of the 70 viewer files once per smell and mixes the viewer with the Python scripts. By-area keeps one surface stable.

alternatives.option: Refactor the whole repo now, Python and cobuilder-memory included, in one epic
alternatives.rejected_because: It widens the blast radius to 129 more files across the plugin families, which ADR-0016's seam keeps separate.

alternatives.option: Leave the viewer's 1,080 comment findings out of the viewer epic
alternatives.rejected_because: They are two thirds of the viewer's findings, so the viewer would never read clean. Per-comment review keeps every comment that explains why.

architecture.narration: The first epic runs in one order, by area. The logic layer comes first, then the atoms and sections, then the change surface, then the shell and chrome, then the test files. The two comment slices come last, because they touch the same files again and need the final structure. Each slice keeps the export surface it touches. A unit that moves out of a large file is re-exported under its old name, so an import of that name still resolves and the test that drives it still runs. After a slice, the engineer re-runs habit-sensors on the files the slice touched. The catalog is the memory between epics. It holds the counts, the clusters, and the verdicts, and it is the one place a later pass reads to cut the second epic into slices.

beats.text: findings-catalog.md under docs/architecture/designs/mechanical-smells/: the scan, the 14 smells with counts, the seven clusters, and a verdict per cluster.
The viewer logic layer: model.ts and the data folder, split by concern, exports kept stable, verified by the vitest suite.
The render layers: atoms.tsx, sections.tsx, panels, the change surface, and the shell and chrome, each split by render unit.
The export surface of model.ts, atoms.tsx, sections.tsx, and App.tsx is the contract. A split keeps every name and re-exports the moved unit.
.habit-hooks/config.toml excludes the generated components/ui and components/smoothui folders, so the scan measures code the team owns.
After the logic slice, a byte-identical rebuild of the committed index.html holds, so a logic split changed no output.
A reviewer samples each comment slice and counts the deleted comments that explained why.
